commitResults.messageTitle: Add deposit and withdraw commands with core structure
commitResults.messageBody: Implement deposit (#8) and withdraw (#9). These are the first features that create transactions, so add the shared base they need: Transaction, TransactionList, Command, Parser, Ui and FinNusException. Other commands (balance, recent, delete, help) can be added as new Command subclasses. Parser accepts parameters in any order, rejects invalid amounts (negative, zero, more than 2 decimals, NaN, scientific notation) and requires a description for withdraw. Add JUnit tests for parsing, commands and Transaction formatting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use BigDecimal for amounts and add no-description deposit constructor
commitResults.messageBody: double cannot represent most decimal values exactly (e.g. 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004), so balances would drift and comparisons could be wrong. BigDecimal keeps amounts exact. Add DepositCommand(BigDecimal) for deposits without a description, as suggested in review. Enable assertions for the Gradle run task.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add deposit and withdraw sections to User Guide
commitResults.messageBody: Document the format, amount rules (positive, at most 2 decimal places, max 1,000,000), optional vs required description, and that parameters can be given in any order. Include examples and expected output so users know what to expect. Replace the template todo example.

The course recommends adding logging to make the code more defensive. Logs go to finnus.log instead of the console, so they never mix with the CLI output the user sees. If the log file cannot be created, logging is turned off instead of stopping the app. Log app start/exit, executed commands, failed commands, parsed input, and added deposits/withdrawals. Ignore log files in git.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add deposit and withdraw section to Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody: The DG was still the template. Document how deposit and withdraw work so future developers can extend them: the classes involved, the step-by-step flow of a withdraw command through Parser and TransactionList, the amount validation rules, and the design alternatives considered (BigDecimal vs double, required vs optional description).
